doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Travels and the Greenwich Village neighborhood
title: What New York does to his creativity
summary: Deadlines help; composing was easier at the house in the woods.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Tell me a little bit about whether the New York… I don’t know, rhythm, feel, atmosphere… does to your artistic sensibilities? Does it feed it, does it dampen it?
Do you want to get away sometimes?

Probably all, all of the above. It’s probably things that I’ve talked about before. When I, when I have… like when I wrote that orchestra piece, I really had to concentrate like mad, and I never did finish it. It was supposed to be piece movements, plural, (laughs) (when?) I squeezed it together. I think in a certain sense it… I’m not sure. I think it had been a bit easier for me to do composition up, up in the woods at the house in Lake Celeste there. But I’m not… If something needs to be done and you have… the term deadline is pretty appropriate, I think. You somehow get it done.
